brief: A workbench organizer: two storeys, bins on top, a drawer below, all edges capped.

requirements.evidence: Level 0: piece:-1,0,0, piece:0,0,0, piece:1,0,0 (half-n). Level 1: piece:-1,0,1 and piece:0,0,1.
bin:0,0,1~hex-bin-full-div3 and bin:-1,0,1~hex-bin-full-div2 sit on the upper storey. A marker, a brush and a pen stand in them as staging.
drawer:0#1,0#cut sits on the half base piece:1,0,0 on the lower storey.
capOpenFaces added 17 solid end caps to the open faces. check_build reports no issues and the mesh check is clear.

finish.summary: Two-storey workbench organizer. The lower storey is a row of three bases: two full bases and a north half base at the east end. A drawer (drawer:0#1,0#cut) sits on the cut face of the half base. The upper storey has two full bases, each holding a full-height divided bin (one split in 3, one in 2). capOpenFaces put 17 solid end caps on the open faces, and lockJoints added two joint bolts. check_build finds no rule issues and the mesh check is clear. A marker, a paint brush and a pen stand in the bins as staging. Several other tools wouldn't stay upright or fit, so they were left out.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
